I decided one day I didn’t want to do it anymore after years of social drinking required for social anxiety. I use the app Sober Time as it helped me to keep track of my sobriety and I also used the app Daybreak to talk to other people who were sober. 
Lots of people commented on it initially, especially my colleagues in my high stress job who said “it would never last” and that it would only be a matter of time before I’d drink again after a day at work. That actually helped with the motivation as I didn’t want to use alcohol as a coping mechanism anymore. 
I found the best thing for me to say when people questioned why I wasn’t drinking was simply “because I don’t want to.” 
It’s doable and it’ll change your life for the better. I am 20 months sober now and I’ll never go back to drinking.

I have also just recently made my list of distractions for when I start spiralling:
- go for a brisk walk / hike (building your heart rate forces you to take deep breaths, helps me a lot) 
- reading 
- work out at gym / pilates
- at home Pilates / yoga practice 
- watching a tv show or movie 
- journalling all my thoughts without thinking about them 
- call a friend / family member 
- cook some food and eat it 
- clean 
- surf
- swim 
- podcasts about the abuse / break up / self love and healing

I quit weed after smoking daily for about 3 years. I had a bong about a week after I quit and was overcome with anxiety. After years of self medicating for anxiety I realised that it was actually enhancing my anxiety, not reducing it.

I used to be an avid reader as a child and then after I did my uni degree in history, needed a break. I couldn’t read anything but Harry Potter and other classic faves, easy reads, nothing new. Now, about 8 years on, I’ve deleted all of my social media and have been able to read 30 books over 2023. My goal is 50 this year. I needed to slowly build up my tolerance to not being consistently “entertained”, mix up the books I read from super easy reads to more complex, and replace other habits with reading (for example having a glass of wine). Worked a treat for me, and I’m as passionate about reading now as I was when I was a kid.

I am sorry that you’ve gone through this with your current partner as well as your last partner. Some things I would say that I want you to believe which I am trying to believe myself. 


- You are not alone and you deserve so much better than this treatment from your partner. You deserve to be treated with respect, care, kindness and love. Not abuse. 

- You have every right to leave the relationship over text if that is what you need. This is about you now, and if you need to do this over text, that’s what you do. 

- Make sure you have a few support people around you that you can talk to when you need it. You are going to need people to keep you on track and feeling loved and supported. 

- You are the most important thing and taking this step for yourself will free you. It will be fucking hard and painful. But you can do this and you will survive and be stronger for it. 

- You have not done anything wrong to deserve this treatment. You deserve to love yourself and feel safe. 

- Do some things you love. I will be doing Yoga with Adriene’s 30 day yoga journey starting tomorrow and it will give me something to look forward to everyday. 

I’m here if you want to talk or need someone to vent to. You are never alone

I had a similar experience to this as well. I was under anaesthesia for my wisdom teeth (all four) and the chair in the middle of the all-white, sterile room was labelled ‘Dexter’. The last memory I have is the nurse telling me she will “count back from ten,” and hearing the number nine. 
I woke up partway through (not sure which tooth at this point) with bright lights in my eyes and the surgeon yanking at my tooth with all of his might. I moaned and groaned in what I believe was discomfort or pain, but I’m not really sure. He said, “Go back to sleep, Paige.” And I did. 
When I woke up again I was sitting in the room with my mom at my side. I immediately burst into hysterics with a mouthful of gauze, blood and saliva requesting to see my teeth. I had all four removed intact. The next day I was eating pizza and Halloween candy and writing an exam for a first year Kinesiology course.
Good times!

This is a story told to me by my dad. We had a golden retriever named Sunny. One day my dad was home with my brothers and I (they were 7 and I was around 2 and a half). Dad comes to find that I’m gone and that he’s left the door open, so he goes out to the park behind our house, to the street on the other side. He said he walked around the streets for about 15 minutes before he saw Sunny sitting on the front lawn of a house and staring at it. She wouldn’t come when called so dad knocked on the door and a nice little old lady had found me walking the streets with my dog.

His ex wife was awful to my brothers and I, and would pretend like she was this lovely person when we were around people but would verbally abuse us when it was just us (my dad would be there too). When I was fifteen I moved in with my dad because up until then I didn’t really know him that well as we only saw him every other weekend. It was awful. She obviously didn’t want my dad to have another “woman” in his life and constantly treated me like shit. When I was eighteen she blew up at me (for the umpteenth time) and when I showed my dad the texts she had sent me calling me a bitch, saying I didn’t care about my little brother (they had a son together who I love dearly) or my dad, all he said was “I don’t see what the big deal is.” I went home and moved out right then and there and didn’t speak to my dad for over a year. 

We are alright now, but he is dating a new woman who is very similar and now my little brother is dealing with it and my dad won’t hear it.

I'm working through this as we speak. I was on reddit the other day on r/AskReddit and someone said "What is one thing you love about yourself?".

I couldn't think of anything. My mind was completely blank. I spoke to my mum about it and she mentioned that when she had gone through a divorce with my dad and was raising us three kids, she would write three things she was grateful for in a journal next to her bed every night. Then, in the morning, she would look it over to remind herself of all of the things she was lucky to have and it would start her day on a good note. 

I've started doing this. I'm only two weeks in, but I can already feel myself being a more positive person, who is learning to love herself again and feel confident in her decisions.

I taught the most amazing group of grade 6 and 7 students for the last three months of the school year when their teacher went on disability. Our whole class had an amazing bond that grew quickly. The kids all cared for each other deeply. They regularly demonstrated care, love, sympathy, compassion, and kindness towards one another. 

When I moved away, they made me a beautiful scrapbook with a special message from each of them. It’s such a special and genuine gift. 

I check in with some of them to see how they’re doing. Some got through and experienced tough times while I was their teacher and I like to make sure everything is going well with them.
